Subject: Request: SLO-preserving deployment policy for upcoming A/B

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re planning an A/B experiment that will gradually shift 30% of production traffic to the new model variant next week. Our compliance team flagged the need for stronger SLA guarantees during the experiment window: OptimaHealth requires an explicit automatic-fallback policy and a version-pinning option so we can guarantee no more than 1 hour of elevated error/latency exposure before rollback.

Concretely, can Redwood provide: 
- An automatic revert if p95 latency increases by more than 40% over baseline for >10 minutes, or if error rate (5xx + latency timeouts) exceeds 0.4% absolute for >5 minutes.
- The ability to pin traffic to the previous model version immediately via API/console (we may require an admin-level rollback toggle).
- A short runbook for our on-call with checks and quick remediation steps.

We’d like confirmation and a proposed policy by EOD so our procurement team can include it in the SOW.

Thanks,
Anita Shah
Head of Product Operations | OptimaHealth

Hi Anita —

Appreciate the clear ask and the SOW timing. Short answer: yes, we can support an SLA-preserving deployment policy that includes automatic fallback and immediate pinning. I’ve sketched a proposed policy below; I’ll loop in ops and product for sign-off and will attach our playbook.

Proposed policy (summary):
- Canary window: ramp to 30% over 30 minutes with progressive steps (5%, 10%, 20%, 30%).
- Automatic revert triggers:
  * p95_latency > baseline_p95 * 1.40 for a rolling 10-minute window -> automatic revert to previous model variant for that region.
  * combined error rate (5xx + timeout) > 0.4% absolute for a rolling 5-minute window -> automatic revert.
- Pinning: admin-level immediate pin to previous model via console/API (role-based access control applies; will provide a one-click rollback toggle for your ops team).
- Safety net: circuit breaker that reduces traffic to 0 for the new variant if traffic surge coincides with threshold breach and automatic revert fails.
- Notification: automatic alert to your DevOps Slack channel + email + an audit log entry with reason and metrics snapshot.

I’ve attached the deployment playbook (redwood_deploy_playbook_v2.md) with the operational steps we expect on both sides. Can I get internal approval and a small confirmation note back to Anita by 2pm PT?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Team —

OptimaHealth has asked for explicit automatic-fallback triggers and an immediate pin/rollback toggle to be included in the SOW for their A/B next week. I’ve proposed the thresholds below (same as in the customer email). Need product/ops sign-off before I confirm to the customer.

Proposed triggers:
- p95 latency > baseline_p95 * 1.40 for rolling 10m -> auto revert.
- Error rate > 0.4% absolute for rolling 5m -> auto revert.
- If auto revert fails to complete within 2 minutes (rare), circuit breaker reduces new-variant traffic to 0 and triggers manual ops playbook.

Operational notes:
- We must ensure the rollback path is idempotent and does not create KV-cache mismatches. Ops: confirm that model variant pinning is available via API and that RBAC can limit toggles to OptimaHealth admins + Redwood SRE.
- Telemetry: telemetry team to provide a per-route metrics snapshot (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, tail-CPU) in the alert payload.

Please reply with APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES. If approve, I’ll send the final policy to Anita and attach the runbook + DocuSign link for SOW appendix.

—Rachel

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Approval needed — OptimaHealth SLO-preserving deploy policy

APPROVE with the following conditions:

1) Tighten the rollback guard: add a secondary condition so that we only trigger auto-revert when both (a) absolute error_rate > 0.4% AND (b) relative error_rate increase > 50% over a 5-minute baseline. This reduces false positives for low-volume routes.
2) Add a cooldown: once revert completes, prevent re-rollforward to the new variant for 30 minutes unless explicitly overridden by OptimaHealth admin.
3) RBAC: require a two-person approval for manual pin overrides when reverting after business-hours.

Ops notes: SRE will validate idempotency and KV-cache behavior; expected work is a 2-hour runbook walkthrough with OptimaHealth on-call before the test. We can meet the notification and telemetry requirements.

Priyom Das
VP, Inference Platform

Hi Anita —

Thanks for the patience. Ops has approved the policy with a couple of additional safety controls we think help both sides avoid noisy reverts: 

Finalized policy (high level):
- Automatic revert triggers (both conditions must be met to trigger):
  1) absolute error rate (5xx + timeouts) > 0.4% AND relative error rate increase > 50% vs 5-minute baseline (to avoid triggering on low-volume noise).
  2) p95 latency > baseline_p95 * 1.40 for a rolling 10-minute window.
- Cooldown: after an automatic revert, the system prevents automatic re-rollforward for 30 minutes unless OptimaHealth admin expressly overrides.
- Pinning: immediate admin-level pin via console/API with audit trail; two-person approval required for after-hours manual overrides.
- Circuit breaker: if auto-revert fails, new-variant traffic is cut to 0 and on-call is paged; the revert attempt remains in the audit log.
- Notifications & telemetry: alert payload contains p50/p95/p99, error-rate, sample request IDs, and a snapshot link to the metrics dashboard.
